english: They helped a friend for a long time.
tip: Duration words like долго (dolga = for a long time) pair with the imperfective: помогали (pamagali = were helping), usually not the perfective.

english: He needs to call the plumber today.
tip: An animate masculine object takes its genitive form: сантехника (santekhnika = plumber) is the object of вызвать (vyzvat = to call).

target: У нас нет молока в холодильнике.
english: We don't have milk in the refrigerator.
tip: The word нет (net = there is no) forces the genitive: молоко (malako = milk) becomes нет молока (net malaka = no milk).

target: Друзья встречаются в кафе по пятницам.
english: Friends meet at the cafe on Fridays.
tip: For repeated days use по (pa) plus the dative plural: по пятницам (pa pyatnitsam = on Fridays), from пятница (pyatnitsa = Friday).

target: Ей нужно купить три килограмма яблок.
english: She needs to buy three kilograms of apples.
tip: After 2, 3, 4 the noun is genitive singular: три килограмма (tri kilagramma = three kilograms), not килограммы (kilagrammy).

english: I will definitely come.
tip: приду (pridu = will come) is a perfective future: one word, no быть (byt = to be). обязательно (abyazatelna = definitely) fits this sense of a sure, completed arrival.

english: He will write a letter.
tip: напишет (napishet = will write) is perfective, so its present-tense ending already means future. No быть (byt = to be) needed, and it frames writing as a single finished act.

english: She often bought dinner.
tip: часто покупала (chasta pakupala = often bought) is imperfective. A frequency word like часто (chasta = often) signals a repeated habit, not one purchase.

english: He bought dinner right away.
tip: сразу купил (srazu kupil = bought right away) is perfective, marking one completed act. сразу (srazu = right away) points to a finished result, so the imperfective would not fit here.

english: I will listen to music.
tip: Imperfective future is быть (byt = to be) plus an infinitive: буду слушать (budu slushat = will listen). It describes ongoing or repeated action, not one finished act.

english: You will write a letter.
tip: будешь писать (budesh pisat = will write) is imperfective future and stresses the process. The perfective напишешь (napishesh) would stress finishing it.

english: He will solve this problem.
tip: решит (reshit = will solve) is perfective future, framing the task as solved once. The imperfective would be будет решать (budet reshat = will be solving), an ongoing effort.

english: When will you finish work?
tip: закончишь (zakonchish = will finish) is perfective, so this present-tense form points to the future. когда (kagda = when) plus a perfective verb asks about one completed moment.

english: I sometimes cooked dinner.
tip: иногда готовил (inagda gatovil = sometimes cooked) is imperfective. Repeated or habitual past actions take the imperfective aspect, marked here by иногда (inagda = sometimes).

english: She often studied the lesson.
tip: часто учила (chasta uchila = often studied) is imperfective for a repeated past habit. A single finished study would use perfective выучила (vyuchila = learned).

english: He memorized the lesson immediately.
tip: сразу выучил (srazu vyuchil = learned immediately) is perfective, so the result is reached. The imperfective учил (uchil = studied) would mean was studying, with no guaranteed finish.

english: You rarely opened the dictionary.
tip: редко открывал (redka atkryval = rarely opened) stays imperfective. A frequency word like редко (redka = rarely) marks a repeated non-event, so the process aspect is used.

english: She often sealed the letter.
tip: часто запечатывала (chasta zapechatyvala = often sealed) is imperfective. The -ыва- (-yva-) stem builds the repeated-action form, matching часто (chasta = often).

english: We say goodbye to friends.
tip: прощаемся с друзьями (prashchayemsya s druzyami = say goodbye to friends): the verb прощаться (prashchatsya) pairs with с (s = with) plus the instrumental case.

english: A white cat is more beautiful than a black one.
tip: красивее чёрной (krasiveye chyornay = more beautiful than a black one): after a comparative, than is shown by putting the compared noun in the genitive, no extra word needed.

english: We spent vacation at the sea.
tip: на море (na more = at the sea): this noun takes на (na = on or at), not в (v = in), for location. Some nouns default to на where English says at or in.

english: He cooked dinner all day.
tip: весь день готовил (ves den gatovil = cooked all day) is imperfective. A time span like весь день (ves den = all day) frames the action as ongoing, so the process aspect is used.

english: We went to the museum yesterday.
tip: ходили (khadili = went) here means a round trip: we went to the museum and came back. That there-and-back sense is built into the verb.

english: The taxi is taking us to the airport.
tip: такси (taksi = taxi) never changes form: it is indeclinable, the same in every case. Here it is the subject doing the carrying, везёт (vezyot = is taking).

target: Она весь вечер писала письмо, но так и не дописала.
english: She wrote a letter all evening but never finished it.
tip: писала (pisala = was writing) is imperfective and says nothing about finishing, so не дописала (ne dapisala = did not finish writing) can follow without contradiction.

english: She takes care of her parents.
tip: своих (svoikh = one's own) points back to the subject: о своих родителях (a svoikh raditelyakh = about her own parents), not someone else's. Use свой (svoy) when the owner is the subject.

english: I often went to the restaurant.
tip: ходила (khadila = went on foot) is the walking verb. For going by vehicle you would say ездила (yezdila = went). English went hides this split.

english: Tomorrow grandfather will wash the dishes at home.
tip: помоет (pamoyet = will wash) is perfective, so the present-tense ending carries future meaning. завтра (zavtra = tomorrow) fits its one-time, finished sense.

english: The dog waits for its owner at the door.
tip: ждёт хозяина (zhdyot khazyaina = waits for the owner): animate masculine nouns take an -а (-a) accusative ending, identical to their genitive form.

target: В следующем году я поеду в Россию.
english: Next year I will go to Russia.
tip: поеду в Россию (payedu v Rassiyu = will go to Russia): to show motion toward a place, use в (v = to or into) plus the accusative case.
